doc.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Sonny Payne and travelling in his Chrysler Imperial
summary: Young says he and drummer Sonny Payne were close pals who drove between gigs in Payne's Chrysler Imperial.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Right, right. So lets talk about your time with the Basie band.
The time in the Basie band before you joined the NBC orchestra. So that time you were with the Basie band in the late 50‘s. From about ‘57…the time you were with the Basie band…
Lets talk about that, about the people you were with because I know you had a good relationship with Sonny Payne.
Good relationship with Sonny Payne, the drummer.
We‘re going to talk about some of those relationships. [laughs]

Sonny Payne and I [laughs], Sonny Payne and I was very close, man. He and I was good pals. Poor Sonny, I‘m sorry he‘s gone, man, I imagine you are, too. You know, Sonny was a hell of a drummer, you know that?
Throwing those sticks up in the air.

Yeah, oh he was something else, man. Sonny Payne and I used to drive, he bought a, he had a, what did he call it now. He had some kind of car and we would travel on the road in his car instead of riding on the bus and everything. We‘d go from the gig in his, I think it was a, what did he have…
I think it was, that‘s right. How did you get that? That‘s what he had, a Chrysler Imperial.
I said that‘s what drummers drive, Chrysler Imperial.
Well, he had a Chrysler Imperial and we would get through the gig and we‘d hit the road to the next town wherever we was going to go, Sonny Payne and I. Sonny Payne…the trumpet player, Thad Jones.
